purpose: Verify Passenger Recovery after a missed connection, including itinerary schedule consistency, passenger delay cost, residual seat capacity, reaccommodation, and UNSERVED fallback.

cost_logic.default_decision: F103 has 40 residual seats, so the 18,000 reaccommodation is cheaper than 50,000 UNSERVED.
cost_logic.low_capacity_decision: F103 has only 10 residual seats. PRM selects passenger groups as indivisible commodities, so the 20-person recovery itinerary violates capacity and UNSERVED is the only schedule-compatible feasible candidate.

manual_checks: Visualization shows F101 as directly affected by the A departure closure; F102 and F103 remain scheduled normally.
F101 is recovered at +60, arriving B at 10:00; original F102 departed B at 09:30, so the original passenger itinerary is unusable.
With 40 residual seats on F103, WB6_PG1 is transported via F101_D60 + F103_ORIG and arrives C at 12:00 (+90 minutes).
Passenger Recovery reports 20 reaccommodated passengers and no unserved passengers in the default-capacity variant.
With F103 residual capacity reduced to 10, the same 20-person group cannot be split and is selected UNSERVED.
Aircraft and crew assignments remain original in both variants.
design_notes: Only the passenger dimension is intended to change between variants; schedule, aircraft and crew data are identical.
The three flights use E1/E2/E3 and matching crew ratings to make resource reassignment structurally impossible and keep this a passenger-specific test.
The original itinerary is retained as an explicit candidate so schedule consistency can reject it after F101_D60 is selected.
No F101_D60 + F102 itinerary is supplied because F102 departs before the delayed F101 arrives at B.
The low-capacity variant tests the current documented PRM behavior of indivisible passenger-group itinerary selection rather than partial splitting.
